canonical.title: Count the number of substrings with k unique characters

narrative.title: Counting Broadcast Windows on Exactly K Channels
narrative.scenario: A spectrum monitor logs a day's broadcast as one long string where each character names the channel a transmitter occupied. Planning needs to know how many contiguous listening windows used exactly K distinct channels — windows are counted by position, so identical content at different offsets counts separately. The monitor answers by counting windows with at most K channels, counting those with at most K-1, and taking the difference.
narrative.inputFormat: A string S of lowercase English letters and an integer K.
narrative.outputFormat: The number of (not necessarily distinct) substrings of S that contain exactly K distinct characters.

testCases.explanation: "ab", "ba" and "aba" each mix exactly two channels.
Six single-character windows plus the "aa" pair — every window with one distinct channel.

hintLevels: Level 1: "Exactly K" is hard to hold directly in a window, but "at most K" is easy — and exactly K is the difference of two at-most counts.
Level 2: Run the standard sliding-window tally for at most K distinct and for at most K-1 distinct; subtracting the two totals answers the question.
Level 3: Shrink from the left whenever the distinct count exceeds K, and add the window length at each step — every right endpoint contributes one count per valid left endpoint that ends there.
